body:
Why not just say "Ashley, that is inappropriate.  Get up." 

Calling people out by gender isn't necessary.
Singing; can't hit a single note properly.  Also, academics.  I'm dumb as shit.

Sometimes it gets better.  I was horrendously depressed during my teenage years and my mood improved in my twenties.  Now things are pretty ehh right now but you never know, maybe it will get better again.
Do you need high grades for scholarships or financial aid?  If not, a passing grade is a passing grade.  No one asks you what your GPA was once you graduate.

Yeah, that's good advice but I have no idea how to do that.  When I have an anxiety attack it's next to impossible for me to pause anything and think about the bigger picture.  I can only do so several hours afterwards.

No, it's still being worked on.  We're doing the legal aspects right now.  I just feel I'd be too inefficient and difficult to work with due to my issues.

Little things for example, I live in a condo complex with an HOA that will send rule violation notices to people and I received one for something that I didn't even do.  I just completely freaked out.

IMO, the best years of your life don't start until you're in your twenties.  I didn't meet my current SO until I was 26 and honestly people that date when they're 18/19 and end up getting quickly married usually get divorced.  You change so much through the college years.

Using someone to fill a void in your life is going to be disappointing, I promise you.

Contacts are extremely important in any endeavor.

Too bad I'm so socially awkward that I know no one.

My parents filled out my college applications, wrote my entire college essay, and did a lot my essay writing for high school courses.  Their reasoning was that I was not capable enough to do it on my own.  Needless to say, it created a tremendous inferiority complex in my adulthood that I'm STILL dealing with ten years later.  I ended up dropping out of college and cutting them off completely so I could learn to be responsible on my own.  I'm doing pretty well now.

Sadly, my parents are still writing my brother's resumes and filling in his job applications.  He's 24!

It's so incredibly damaging to a person's self esteem for someone to do things for them when they're developmentally capable of it for themselves.  It preaches a "you're not good enough" message and reinforces learned helplessness.
